verdict.rationale: Smithery's docs say published servers get a dedicated server page where users can "discover, try, and install" the MCP. That is a glancing, first-party hint at in-browser trial of a server, but nothing describes an inspector or playground for calling tools. The CLI's `smithery tool call` is a command-line surface, not a browser one, so it earns no credit here. The October 2026 shutdown of Smithery's hosted Connect services also leaves it unclear whether any in-browser trial still works. Missing for 10: an explicitly documented browser-based inspector or playground for invoking tools, details of how tool calls are run and shown in the browser, confirmation it survived the shutdown, and hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can exercise an MCP server's tools from a browser-based inspector or playground before integrating it

citations.quote: Get a dedicated server page where users can discover, try, and install your MCP from any client
